candidate_relations.reason: Soft-tissue nodules within an adrenal-region fatty mass are characteristic of myelolipoma rather than pure lipoma.
The lesion was predominantly macroscopic fat, not a solid lipid-rich cortical adenoma.
A 15.6-cm adrenal-site mass with interspersed enhancing myeloid tissue is not an ordinary lipoma.
Ultrasound showed minimal vascularity and cross-sectional imaging was dominated by fat rather than vascular channels.
A well-circumscribed noninvasive adrenal-region mass combining macroscopic fat and enhancing soft tissue is diagnostic of adrenal myelolipoma.
The histologic tumor type is compatible, but the label does not retain the case-defining right adrenal anatomy.
MRI established an extra-renal lesion displacing the right kidney, with no renal origin described.
Hibernoma is typically avidly enhancing, whereas this encapsulated adrenal mass had mostly fat density and minimal vascularity.
No calcification, teeth, fluid, or other mixed germ-layer components were present.
Smooth encapsulation, organ displacement without invasion, and adrenal location argue against retroperitoneal liposarcoma.
The patient was 48 and the mass was fat-rich, unlike a solid catecholamine-producing neuroblastoma.
Electrophoresis documented beta-thalassemia trait, which explains chronic microcytosis but not the adrenal mass.
The lesion lacked the cystic, calcified, and heterogeneous germ-layer architecture of a teratoma.
